newsitem.title: SPAIN: Mapfre sees foreign business boosting share.
newsitem.headline: Mapfre sees foreign business boosting share.

text.p: Spanish insurance firm Corporacion Mapfre's foreign business is the key to a recovery in its share price, general manager Domingo Sugranyes told journalists on Friday.
"Probably, when the international business improves this will be definitively reflected in the share price," Sugranyes said.
From the start of the year, Mapfre shares have fallen around 7.3 percent on the stock market, while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares has risen around 22 percent.
At 1220 GMT Mapfre was lower 10 pesetas to 6.290 pta.
Sugranyes said he understood investor caution after the fir surprised the market by issuing 16 billion pesetas in convertible bonds in February, more than expected.
The issue was aimed at financing Latin American investments, he added.
"It was the right moment to do it," he said. These investments might take time to bear fruit, Sugranyes added.

Mapfre Internacional director, Javier Palacios said he was expecting net profit from Mapfre Internacional this year to rise versus last year's 1,3 billion pesetas, with total investment of 39 billion pesetas and premium of 96 billion.

In 1996, Mapfre investments in Latin America will total rise up to 45 billion pesetas. The company has bought the Venezuela's largest insurance company Seguros la Seguridad, paying around 3.5 billion and 3.8 billion pesetas. Mapfre bought also the peruan El Sol Nacional.
Total premium are set to rise to 120 billion pesetas.
